name: Speak Up. Take Action.
pressTitle: TO VIMA / Students take a stand against bullying
location: 56th Junior High School of Athens, Greece
brief: An independently funded film created to start a conversation about school bullying, made with the students of the 56th Junior High School of Athens. Producer Boris Anchev returned to his former school to make the studio's first production a project with a social purpose. Released around Greece's National Day Against School Violence and Bullying on 6 March, the film asks a direct question: what changes when the people who witness bullying choose to speak up?
approach: Directed by George Stamou, the film uses repetition to reveal how everyday bullying becomes normalised. Five recurring situations move through the rhythms of school life, while classmates look on, laugh or remain silent. When the pattern breaks, an absence makes the consequences impossible to ignore. Rather than treating bullying as an isolated confrontation, the story turns its attention to the bystander and the choice between silence and support.
production: The school's classrooms, corridors and courtyard became a working film set across four days of rehearsals and filming. First- and second-year students participated alongside the production team, bringing the message into the spaces they use every day. The project was funded by Boris Anchev and realised with the support of school principal Tasos Karabinis. The accompanying behind-the-scenes film documents the collaboration between the students and crew.
